corpus: 13 arXiv papers on context engineering and long-context language models, concatenated in a fixed order (see code/studio-02/corpus/manifest.json); combined length ~579K o200k tokens (combined_real_tokens per manifest.json).
corpus_note: Documents in combined.txt order: (1) Mei et al. 2025, A Survey of Context Engineering for LLMs, arXiv 2507.13334 -- prose ends ~41K tokens in, the remainder to ~145K is bibliography with no facts; (2) Liu et al. 2023, Lost in the Middle, 2307.03172; (3) Packer et al. 2023, MemGPT, 2310.08560; (4) Zhang et al. 2025, ACE: Agentic Context Engineering, 2510.04618; (5) Hsieh et al. 2024, RULER, 2404.06654; (6) Wu et al. 2024, LongMemEval, 2410.10813; (7) Yao et al. 2022, ReAct, 2210.03629; (8) Lewis et al. 2020, RAG, 2005.11401; (9) Park et al. 2023, Generative Agents, 2304.03442; (10) Modarressi et al. 2025, NoLiMa, 2502.05167; (11) Mem0, 2504.19413; (12) Brown et al. 2020, GPT-3, 2005.14165; (13) Gemini 1.5 technical report, 2403.05530. Questions 1-5 are drawn from document 1's prose (all within the first ~41K tokens). Questions 6-15 are 10 answerable needles spread across documents 2-6 (reachable within a 256K-token slice); questions 16-17 are 2 answerable needles in documents 7 and 9 (beyond 256K, reachable only via Part B's per-document isolation); questions 18-20 are plausible questions whose answers are not present anywhere in the corpus (expect_not_found=true; needle_depth_tokens is null for these three -- see lib/charts.py and lib/pi_runner.py, which key expected-verdict and heatmap-row-labeling off expect_not_found directly and treat a null depth as "not in corpus"). needle_depth_tokens for questions 6-17 was measured directly against the real code/studio-02/corpus/combined.txt (tiktoken o200k_base tokens preceding the first -- or, for the one multi-hop question, the second/deeper -- occurrence of the fact).

questions.question: According to the survey's abstract, how many research papers does the survey analyze?
questions.doc_title: A Survey of Context Engineering for LLMs (Mei 2025)
questions.verification: grep -Eio 'over[^.]{0,20}1,?400 research papers' survey.txt  # 2 hits: Abstract and Conclusion

questions.question: According to the survey, what maximum context window does LongRoPE achieve, and how (in how many stages)?
questions.gold_answer: LongRoPE achieves 2048K tokens (about 2 million tokens), via a two-stage approach: fine-tune to 256K length, then positional interpolation to the maximum length
questions.section_hint: Section 4, Position Interpolation and Context Extension (page ~18)
questions.doc_title: A Survey of Context Engineering for LLMs (Mei 2025)
questions.verification: grep -Eio 'LongRoPE achieves 2048K token context windows through two-stage approaches' survey.txt  # 1 genuine hit in prose; 2 further hits elsewhere are bibliography citation titles for an unrelated LongRoPE paper, not restatements of this claim

questions.question: According to the survey, what percentage improvement does GPT-4 achieve through iterative self-refinement (the Self-Refine method)?
questions.doc_title: A Survey of Context Engineering for LLMs (Mei 2025)
questions.verification: grep -Eio 'approximately 20% improvement through (iterative )?self-refinement' survey.txt  # 2 hits

questions.question: According to the GAIA benchmark results cited in the survey's evaluation section, what accuracy do humans achieve on general assistant tasks, and what accuracy do advanced models like GPT-4 achieve?
questions.gold_answer: humans achieve 92% accuracy; GPT-4 (advanced models) achieve only 15% accuracy
questions.doc_title: A Survey of Context Engineering for LLMs (Mei 2025)
questions.verification: grep -Eio 'GAIA[^.]{0,200}15%|92%[^.]{0,150}15%' survey.txt  # 3 hits, GAIA human-vs-model comparison restated 3x

questions.question: According to the survey's conclusion, what are the four categories of System Implementations?
questions.gold_answer: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), Memory Systems, Tool-Integrated Reasoning, and Multi-Agent Systems
questions.doc_title: A Survey of Context Engineering for LLMs (Mei 2025)
questions.verification: grep -Ezo 'Retrieval-Augmented Generation[\s\S]{0,400}?Multi-Agent Systems' survey.txt  # 3 hits: abstract, intro roadmap, conclusion

questions.question: According to Lost in the Middle, what is GPT-3.5-Turbo's accuracy in the closed-book setting (no documents given) on the multi-document question answering task?
questions.verification: grep -n '56\.1%' 2307.03172.txt  # Table 1 row 'GPT-3.5-Turbo 56.1% 88.3%'; restated in the intro preview and in the S2.3 results prose (3 genuine hits; 4th whole-doc hit at the unrelated Claude-1.3(100K) row in Appendix Table G.3 is coincidental, different fact)

questions.question: According to Lost in the Middle, what shape does model accuracy follow as the position of the answer-containing document moves from the start of the context to the middle to the end, and where is performance best versus worst?
questions.gold_answer: A U-shaped curve: accuracy is highest when the relevant document is at the very beginning (primacy bias) or end (recency bias) of the input context, and drops significantly when it is in the middle of the context.
questions.verification: grep -c -i 'U-shaped' 2307.03172.txt  # 13 hits (abstract, Fig.1/Fig.5 captions, S2.3 results, GPT-4 and Llama-2 appendices, discussion)

questions.question: According to MemGPT's implementation details, what is the context window size, in tokens, of the gpt-4-0613 endpoint (the model the paper calls 'GPT-4')?
questions.verification: grep -n '8, 192' 2310.08560.txt  # ‘GPT-4‘ refers to gpt-4-0613 (context window of 8, 192), and ‘GPT-3.5 Turbo‘ ... 16, 385; GPT-4 Turbo/gpt-4-1106-preview elsewhere in same paragraph = 128, 000

questions.question: According to MemGPT, what three components make up the LLM's 'main context' (its prompt tokens), as shown in Figure 3?
questions.gold_answer: The system instructions, the working context, and a FIFO queue.
questions.verification: grep -n 'system instructions, working context, and a FIFO' 2310.08560.txt  # Figure 3 caption / S2 architecture description, stated once

questions.question: According to ACE's key findings, by what average percentage does ACE outperform strong baselines on agent benchmarks such as AppWorld?
questions.verification: grep -n '10.6%' 2510.04618.txt  # Abstract, Key Findings bullet, and S4 ReAct+ACE results paragraph (3 hits); 8.6% is the paired finance/domain-specific gain stated alongside each time

questions.question: According to ACE, what does the AppWorld metric 'TGC' stand for, and by what percentage does ReAct+ACE (with online adaptation) surpass the IBM CUGA agent on this metric on the test-challenge split?
questions.gold_answer: TGC stands for Task Goal Completion; with online adaptation, ReAct+ACE surpasses IBM CUGA by 8.4% on TGC on the test-challenge split.
questions.verification: grep -n 'Task' 2510.04618.txt | grep 'Goal Completion'  # TGC/SGC defined once (Evaluation Metrics, S4); grep -n '8.4% in TGC' 2510.04618.txt  # specific figure given once, later, in the AppWorld-leaderboard paragraph (S4.1) -- two separate locations, needle depth uses the deeper (numeric) one

questions.question: According to RULER, what are the four task categories the benchmark is organized into?

Aggregation:\|Question Answering: we add' 2404.06654.txt  # S1 enumerated list; needle depth uses item 4 (Question Answering), the last piece needed to complete the list -- Table 1 is interleaved between items 3 and 4 in the extracted text

questions.verification: grep -n '17 long-context' 2404.06654.txt  # 4 hits (abstract, key findings, models&setup, main results); each pairs '17 models' with '13 tasks' -- 13 is the easy swap

questions.question: According to LongMemEval, what does the 'Abstention' ability require a chat assistant to do?
questions.gold_answer: Identify questions that ask about information never mentioned anywhere in the interaction history (unknown information), and answer "I don't know" rather than fabricate an answer.
questions.verification: grep -n 'Abstention (ABS): Ability to identify questions seeking unknown information' 2410.10813.txt  # S3.2, five-core-abilities bullet list, stated once

questions.question: According to ReAct, by what absolute success-rate margin does it outperform imitation- and reinforcement-learning baselines on the ALFWorld benchmark?
questions.verification: grep -n '34% and 10%' 2210.03629.txt  # Abstract and S1 restate '34% and 10% respectively' for ALFWorld and WebShop respectively

questions.question: According to Generative Agents, what is the name of the sandbox town, inspired by The Sims, that the generative agents inhabit?
questions.verification: grep -c 'Smallville' 2304.03442.txt  # 21 hits; first at 'This sprite-based sandbox game world, Smallville, evokes...' contrasted with 'Sims' (the inspiration, not the name)

questions.question: According to Lost in the Middle, what accuracy does GPT-4 achieve on the multi-document QA task when 30 total documents are retrieved?
questions.gold_answer: NOT FOUND — the paper evaluates GPT-4 only on a subset of the multi-document QA task using 20 total retrieved documents (citing a ~$6000 cost estimate for running the full sweep across all document counts); no 30-document result for GPT-4 is reported anywhere in the paper.
questions.verification: grep -n -i 'gpt-4' 2307.03172.txt  # all 8 mentions checked by hand: S1 footnote and Appendix D both fix the subset at '20 total documents' ($6000 cost note); grep -i 'gpt-4' 2307.03172.txt | grep '30'  # 0 matches

questions.question: According to these 13 papers, how many parameters does GPT-4 have?
questions.gold_answer: NOT FOUND — none of the 13 papers states GPT-4's parameter count; several discuss its context window or usage (e.g., MemGPT gives gpt-4-0613's context window as 8,192 tokens) but OpenAI has never publicly disclosed GPT-4's parameter count, and no paper in the corpus states or estimates it.
questions.verification: grep -n -i 'GPT-4' combined.txt | grep -i 'parameter\|billion'  # 0 matches across the whole corpus; contrast with GPT-3's own disclosed 175B (doc 12), the tempting but wrong distractor

questions.question: According to the GPT-3 paper's Energy Usage section, how many metric tons of CO2 were emitted by training GPT-3?
questions.gold_answer: NOT FOUND — Section 6.3 (Energy Usage) quantifies GPT-3's training compute in petaflop/s-days and gives an inference-cost figure of about 0.4 kW-hr per 100 pages of generated text, but never states a carbon-emissions or CO2 figure for either training or inference.
questions.verification: grep -n -i 'carbon\|CO2\|kWh\|energy consumption' combined.txt  # only 1 whole-corpus hit, a bibliography citation TITLE (not a reported figure); grep -n -i 'carbon\|CO2' 2005.14165.txt  # 0 matches in GPT-3's own text (S6.3 gives only petaflop/s-days and the unrelated 0.4 kW-hr inference figure -- an inference cost a hallucinating answer might wrongly repurpose as a training-CO2 number)
